evals.prompt: Add an MCP tool `check_update` to awg-manager that tells an agent whether a newer awg-manager version is available (the daemon already has an update checker behind GET /api/system/update/check — see internal/api/update*.go and the updater service). Read-only; applying the update must stay out of MCP. Cover it with tests and run them.
evals.expected_output: A read-only tool wired through types/deps/tool/fake/localdeps/scope with tests in both packages, catalogue and scope lists updated, adapter tests actually run in the Linux container.
assertions: Tool registered: changes.patch adds an mcp.AddTool call whose Name is the requested tool
Deps interface extended: changes.patch adds a new method to the Deps interface in internal/mcp/deps.go
Fake implements it: changes.patch adds a matching method on *Fake in internal/mcp/mcptest/fake.go
Adapter implements it: changes.patch adds a matching method on *Local in internal/mcp/localdeps/localdeps.go
Tool-level test exists: changes.patch adds a test in internal/mcp/*_test.go that calls the new tool through callTool
Adapter test exists: changes.patch adds a test in internal/mcp/localdeps/localdeps_test.go exercising the new *Local method
Catalogue updated: changes.patch adds the tool name to the want list in TestServer_ListsToolsWithAnnotations
Native tests passed: tests.log shows `ok` for internal/mcp (go test on the host)
Adapter tests actually RUN in Linux: tests.log or summary.md shows the docker run with `ok ... internal/mcp/localdeps`, not only GOOS=linux vet
Honest test reporting: summary.md does not claim a test passed that tests.log does not show passing
Annotated read-only: the AddTool call uses readOnly(...)
Scope list updated: changes.patch adds `check_update` to readOnlyTools in internal/mcp/scope.go
No apply path: changes.patch adds no tool or Deps method that triggers an update install
Result says what it means: output type has jsonschema descriptions that state whether an update is available and what version, not just raw struct fields
Wired into the daemon: changes.patch passes the updater into localdeps.Config from internal/server/server_routes.go using a concrete type with a nil check

evals.prompt: We need `delete_singbox_rule` in the awg-manager MCP server: delete one sing-box router rule by index. Same staging semantics as set_singbox_rule_outbound (it lands in the draft). Return the deleted rule so the agent can show the user what it removed. Tests please, and run them.
evals.expected_output: A destructive-annotated staged write that refuses managed rules, returns the deleted rule, attaches the staged-notice text, is NOT in the read-only scope, with tests in both packages and the catalogue updated.
assertions: Tool registered: changes.patch adds an mcp.AddTool call whose Name is the requested tool
Deps interface extended: changes.patch adds a new method to the Deps interface in internal/mcp/deps.go
Fake implements it: changes.patch adds a matching method on *Fake in internal/mcp/mcptest/fake.go
Adapter implements it: changes.patch adds a matching method on *Local in internal/mcp/localdeps/localdeps.go
Tool-level test exists: changes.patch adds a test in internal/mcp/*_test.go that calls the new tool through callTool
Adapter test exists: changes.patch adds a test in internal/mcp/localdeps/localdeps_test.go exercising the new *Local method
Catalogue updated: changes.patch adds the tool name to the want list in TestServer_ListsToolsWithAnnotations
Native tests passed: tests.log shows `ok` for internal/mcp (go test on the host)
Adapter tests actually RUN in Linux: tests.log or summary.md shows the docker run with `ok ... internal/mcp/localdeps`, not only GOOS=linux vet
Honest test reporting: summary.md does not claim a test passed that tests.log does not show passing
Annotated destructive: the AddTool call uses destructiveWrite(...)
Not in read-only scope: changes.patch does NOT add `delete_singbox_rule` to readOnlyTools
Returns the deleted rule: the output type carries the removed rule's summary/outbound and a test asserts it
Refuses managed rules: a test shows deleting a rule with managed=true is a tool error, and the adapter checks AwgmManaged before calling the service
